title: Extraction provider client contract v2
description: Successor of extraction_provider_client_contract@0.1.0 (ADR-043, E-M). The released @0.1.0 schema is byte-identical and untouched: its model_parameters object is closed, so thinking_config could not be added there and lives at the top level here instead. This contract declares a two-operation execution shape - countTokens followed by generateContent - with its own timeout, its own retry cap, an exact-equality endpoint grammar, and the canonical six-field generation-config projection that countTokens and generateContent must share. generate_retry_max_attempts and external_request_max are STRUCTURAL maxima; a run's effective cap is derived from live_call_authorization@0.2.0 and may only narrow them. It carries no credential, key, token, header, or account identifier.

operation_endpoint.comment: Exact operation URL. The positive predicate and the negative predicates are kept apart on purpose: a JSON Schema pattern is a SEARCH, and an anchored $ also matches before a trailing newline, so a single anchored rule would admit a URL with a newline appended.

sdk_version.comment: Exact pin. A range would let a resolved runtime differ from the audited one.

model_parameters.comment: Unchanged from @0.1.0 and still closed. thinking_config is NOT here: widening this object would have been a mutation of the released shape.

count_timeout_duration.comment: A declared policy value, not a measurement: 300s was derived for generateContent and was never measured for countTokens. The builder additionally binds it to timeout_duration so the two cannot drift.

count_retry_max_attempts.comment: countTokens is exactly one send. There is no retry: an empty or malformed body is not a declared retry trigger.

generate_retry_max_attempts.comment: STRUCTURAL maximum of the connector. A run's effective cap is min(this, budget_max_external_requests - 1) and may only be narrower.

external_request_max.comment: STRUCTURAL maximum = 1 count send + generate_retry_max_attempts. Never a per-run budget.

thinking_config.comment: Exactly what both operations send. thinking_level and include_thoughts are absent by construction, not merely null: the object is closed and declares one property.

thinking_level_used.comment: A record, never evidence. Absence is proven by a structural test over the serialized request body, not by this flag.

wire_thinking_budget_key.comment: Measured against google-genai 2.13.0: the converter passes the ThinkingConfig through and convert_to_dict does not apply aliases, so the terminal wire body carries snake_case thinking_budget, not thinkingBudget.

generation_config_projection.comment: One canonical fixed ordering. An items.enum plus uniqueItems construction would have admitted every permutation, and a permuted list serializes to different canonical bytes - sort_keys orders dict keys, never list elements - so two semantically identical contracts would have acquired divergent provenance digests.

operation_endpoints.comment: Exactly two named endpoints. A prefix allowlist is no longer accepted: a broad prefix entry admits other publishers, locations and operations at a segment boundary.

protocol_switch_policy.comment: Measured: httpcore breaks its receive loop on a 101 InformationalResponse, so a 101 reaches the send boundary, and the released capture guard only refuses 3xx. The v2 capture refuses a protocol switch before touching response.content.
